body:
Coordinator slip (Termal::Fable2, 2026-11-11 09:08Z, my own miss). I issued a termal_send_to_session whose body was only "placeholder" to host:e83d08f4…::session-4 (the DL560 Engram Runner) in the same parallel batch as a real reply. It was durably delivered as relay #166. I corrected it at once with #167 ("please IGNORE #166"). Rule: never issue a send as a placeholder or no-op, even when it seems harmless. Every send is durable and wakes a real agent. Decide the exact recipient and body before issuing it. For a relay sender, reply to the exact host-qualified native session that wrote the message (here the Mac runner host:abf8bda6…::session-6201), not to another runner with a similar name.

Second slip, same day, ~09:21Z: I sent Sol-a7bb #3051 citing "w-dd??" because I issued engram add and the send in the SAME parallel batch, before the new ref existed. I corrected it at once with #3052 (w-277b7077a6ac). Rule: a message that cites an item I am filing must be sent only AFTER the add returns, in a later step and never in the same batch. This is the existing "file an engram item BEFORE citing its id" rule applied to batching.

Third slip, same day, ~10:02Z: I issued termal_acknowledge_mailbox with receipt "PLACEHOLDER" in the SAME batch as the termal_read_mailbox that would return the real receipt. TermAl refused it with 400, so there was no harm. I then acknowledged with the real receipt. General rule: any call whose argument depends on another call's output (a new item ref, a mailbox receipt, an id) goes in a LATER step, never in the same parallel batch, and never with a placeholder value.
